Expectation1: Ensuring financial stability for the family
Situation1: The child has been promised a Nintendo, and the father should purchase it
Situation2: Your friend has misunderstood the tone of your text message and replied sounding hurt. You need to call them right now to explain.
Story: I sat at the kitchen table, my phone buzzing with a new message from my friend, Mark. His words stung—he thought I was angry with him, all because of a rushed text I’d sent earlier. I knew I should call him right away, clear things up before the misunderstanding grew. But across the room, my son bounced with excitement, clutching the Nintendo catalog. I’d promised him that game console weeks ago, and today was the day I was supposed to buy it. The problem was, money was tight this month, and I’d been counting every dollar to make sure we stayed afloat. My son’s hopeful eyes met mine, full of trust, while my phone vibrated again, Mark’s name lighting up the screen. I felt torn—my son expected me to keep my promise and provide, but my friend needed me to be there, to explain and mend our friendship. The weight of both expectations pressed on me, and I sat frozen, heart pounding, unsure which role to answer first.
